question: If 20% of a number is added to 60, then the result is the same number. 80% of the same number is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the complete number be 100%.

According to the question: 20% of the number + 60 = 100% of the number.

⇒ 100% − 20% = 60

⇒ 80% of the number = 60

The question directly asks for 80% of the same number, which is exactly 60.

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

20% of a number + 60 = the number

**Concept Used:**

Any complete quantity is always considered as 100% of itself.

 
 
 
• 
 20%
 80% = 60
 

 100% (The Complete Number)
 

 Added Value = 60

**Calculations:**

Let the unknown number be x.

⇒ 20% of x + 60 = x

⇒ (20 ÷ 100) × x + 60 = x

⇒ x − 0.20x = 60

⇒ x(1 − 0.20) = 60

⇒ 0.80x = 60

⇒ 80% of x = 60

Since the question asks us to find 80% of the same number, we already have the required value.

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base Value in Percentages

Every quantity in its original or complete state is always considered as 100%. When a part is given as p%, the remaining part is simply (100 − p)%.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Fractions can be easily converted to percentages by multiplying by 100. For example, 1/5 × 100 = 20%, and 4/5 × 100 = 80%.
